{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B keeps a clean chronology from 巨鹿 through 鸿门宴, 分封, 楚汉相争 and 垓下 to 乌江, while Draft A's section three describes 分封 before 鸿门宴, reversing their order."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B has a dedicated 性格分析 section that ties each trait (勇猛, 重情, 刚愎, 残暴) to concrete episodes like 范增, 屠城焚宫 and 坑降卒, whereas Draft A lists traits with few matching examples."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B gives separate, evidence-backed reasons for success and failure (战略失误, 人才流失, 民心渐失, 后勤, 用人失当, 与刘邦对比) with clear conclusions, while Draft A offers only a single generic paragraph."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B devotes sections to historical standing and to later influence, citing 李白, 杜牧 and 京剧《霸王别姬》 to trace the literary and dramatic afterlife, while Draft A's treatment is brief and its 关公/岳飞 comparisons are loosely argued."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B's claims are mostly anchored to 《史记》 quotations and verifiable figures, whereas Draft A misattributes 千金一诺 to 项羽 and includes loosely supported comparisons."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B renders 巨鹿, 鸿门宴 and 垓下 with vivid scenes and dialogue and places measured commentary at the turning points, while Draft A stays dry and summary-like."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B is written in screenplay form with scene headings, action lines, and dialogue across a clear four-act structure, while Draft A is an outline with no actual script format or dialogue."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A states Lin Yu's age, role, and family-victim motive and reuses that motive as a driver across all eight episodes, whereas Draft B establishes it briefly and drops it after the second scene."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A explicitly portrays the villain as seasoned and skilled at disguise, with a public-versus-private contrast ('表面光鲜亮丽，实则心狠手辣'), while Draft B shows his power and age but barely depicts his duplicity."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A lays out Lao Li's fear, refusal, gradual persuasion by Lin Yu, and eventual voluntary help over an episode, giving a more credible psychological arc than Draft B's compressed scenes."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A explicitly contrasts the prosperous city with slums, introduces the investigation through a specific event, and covers undercover work, Lao Li, threats, and framing, though neither draft depicts bribery attempts on Lin Yu."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A covers the punishment of the corrupt, the city's rebuilding, the victims' compensation, and a closing reflection on the endless anti-corruption struggle, whereas Draft B shows only an arrest and a closing narration with little depiction of reconstruction."}, {"id": "r7", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B shows concrete evidence and mechanisms (tender documents, bribe money, payment ledgers, kickback records, meeting recordings) building into a chain, while Draft A only describes such details in generic, hedged terms ('可能')."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A follows the sequence from early life through 起兵, 巨鹿, 鸿门宴, 分封, 楚汉, 垓下 to 乌江 in clear order, while Draft B's thematic sections blur the timing (for example, 巨鹿 in 207 appears before 鸿门宴 in 206)."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A has a dedicated 性格分析 section that names 勇猛, 重情, 刚愎, 贵族心态 and 残暴 and ties several of them to concrete episodes, whereas Draft B covers character in a short summary with little per-trait evidence."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A separately lists the reasons for failure (战略失误, 人才流失, 民心渐失, 政治短视, 用人失当) with supporting episodes and a 成败原因 section, while Draft B gives only a brief unsupported summary of causes."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A discusses posterity in more depth, covering 李白, 杜牧, 京剧《霸王别姬》 and the shift from history to cultural symbol, though it leans toward one-sided praise, while Draft B is thin and mostly one-note."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A's key claims and quotations track 《史记》 closely, while Draft B contains unsupported figures such as '亲率八万楚军' and misattributes the 千金一诺 story (which belongs to 季布) to 项羽."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A renders scenes such as 宋义被杀, 垓下 and 霸王别姬 vividly and adds restrained analysis at the turning points, whereas Draft B reads as a dry summary with little scene-setting."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A follows youth, Julu, the 206 partition, Chu-Han, Gaixia, and Wujiang in clean sequence, while Draft B places the Hongmen banquet after the partition, which is out of order."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A ties personality traits to concrete episodes such as the assassination of Song Yi, the massacre at Xianyang, Pengcheng, and the refusal to cross the river, whereas Draft B stays generic with few specific examples."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A supports its reasons for success and failure with specific events (the Fan Zeng dismissal, Chen Ping's double agent plot, the loss of allies, supply problems, and the contrast with Liu Bang), while Draft B relies on vague assertions like 'historians generally believe'."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A names specific later works and authors (Shiji's Xiang Yu Benji, Li Bai, Li Qingzhao, the opera Farewell My Concubine) and presents both admiration and criticism, while Draft B is more abstract and does not cover the Wujiang evaluations in depth."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A quotes lines that trace to the Shiji, though it states Yu Ji's suicide as fact, which the Shiji does not record, while Draft B hedges with 'speculation' and 'legend' but offers almost no traceable sources."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A uses vivid narration with restrained commentary at turning points such as Julu, Gaixia, and Wujiang, whereas Draft B reads as an abstract, moralizing essay with little scene-building."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A narrates the life in clear chronological stages (早年, 巨鹿, 鸿门, 楚汉, 垓下, 乌江) without reversal, while Draft B's summary sections are chronological only in a brief overview and contain a misattributed event (killing 秦二世 and 赵高)."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A has a dedicated personality section that ties traits such as impetuosity, loyalty and indecision to specific episodes like 鸿门宴, 范增, 分封 and 破釜沉舟, whereas Draft B only asserts traits with little concrete textual support."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A gives a fuller treatment of the causes of success and failure, with explicit conclusions and comparison with 刘邦, though its evidence is thin; Draft B lists reasons in bullet form but with vague, unsupported explanations."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A evaluates historical status across military, cultural and ideological dimensions, cites 司马迁's judgment and later poets (李清照, 杜牧), and includes a critical 历史反思, whereas Draft B offers only generic one-line praise."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A's narrative stays close to 《史记》 wording and avoids the factual errors found in Draft B, though it does not explicitly label its own inferences as speculation."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A uses vivid scene description (宋义停驻四十六天, 破釜沉舟, 四面楚歌, 乌江) with restrained analysis at turning points, while Draft B reads as a dry outline with little narrative vividness."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "B", "why": "B narrates strictly in dated chronological order from birth through Wu Jiang's suicide, with consistent year markers, while A is mostly sequential but drifts into topical analysis sections."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "B", "why": "B has a dedicated character section that ties its traits to concrete Shiji episodes such as the killing of Song Yi, the massacre at Xianyang and Xin'an, and the boiling of the advisor who mocked him, whereas A gives only generic traits with few specific source examples."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "B", "why": "B supports both its rise (Julu, the kneeling generals, the enfeoffment) and its fall (the Xianyang massacre, the failed enfeoffment, the loss of Fan Zeng, the Pengcheng reversal, the isolation at Gaixia) with specific episodes and a clear conclusion, while A's causes are asserted more generally."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "B", "why": "B names concrete later reception (Li Bai, Li Qingzhao, Peking opera) and balances admiration with criticism, though its claim that Han policy was shaped by reflection on Xiang Yu is an unflagged inference and its 'first non-emperor in 本纪' framing is overstated."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "B", "why": "B quotes and dates its claims against Shiji more concretely than A, though it contains a few errors (the advisor's name 韩生 is not in Shiji, the Li Bai attribution is doubtful, and Xiang Liang's death is loosely described) and does not flag speculation or source contradictions."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "B", "why": "B's narration is more vivid, with scenes such as the Qin emperor's southern tour, the Gaixia song, and the Wujiang dialogue, and it keeps commentary mostly at turning points, though it omits Hongmen and its prose is sometimes overly ornate."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B follows the sequence from youth and the uprising through Julu, Hongmen, Pengcheng, Gaixia and Wujiang, while Draft A is organized by topic and states Xiang Yu's capture of Xianyang in 208 BCE, which is out of order."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B ties its character traits to concrete episodes such as Julu's burning of the boats, Hongmen's hesitation and Fan Zeng's advice, and the enfeoffment, whereas Draft A's personality section is generic and cites almost no specific events."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B supports its causes of success and failure with episodes such as Julu, Hongmen and the enfeoffment, while Draft A's numbered causes are asserted without evidence, though its list is clearly labeled."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B covers historical position, military and literary influence, and cites Sima Qian, Li Qingzhao and Du Mu, while Draft A's section is brief and generic."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft A gives Xiang Yu's age at death as 37 (Shiji says 31) and wrongly credits him with killing Zhao Gao, while Draft B's quotations and figures such as the 31 years and the 3,000-versus-560,000 Pengcheng battle match the sources."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B renders the Hongmen, Gaixia and Wujiang turning points as vivid scenes with direct speech and adds restrained commentary, while Draft A reads as a dry, list-like summary."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "tie", "why": "Both drafts give the exact title 海水养殖动物病害病原的分离鉴定及结果分析 near the top of the report, though each adds a preamble first."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A lists reagents, equipment, and culture conditions (28℃, TSA/TCBS, 24–48 h) for the sample handling and bacterial steps, while Draft B gives fewer reagents and no equipment list in the aligned passages."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A gives each pathogen group a full section with biochemical items and judgment, PCR reaction system, cycling, and controls, and parasite morphometric observation, though it wrongly cites 28℃ for API 20E and uses ultrathin sections rather than negative staining."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A reports all three cases with specific results (Gram-negative short rod, WSSV band with negative and marker controls, Trichodina diameter and ring structures), whereas Draft B's aligned results cover only the Gram stain."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A explains causes, ties PCR specificity to controls, and states limitations requiring challenge tests and 16S sequencing, while Draft B's discussion mostly lists findings and overclaims reliability."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "tie", "why": "Both drafts are written in Chinese prose and keep Latin names and English test abbreviations as permitted."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "tie", "why": "Both drafts follow the required chronology from early life through the uprising, Julu, Hongmen, the division of the empire, the Chu-Han war, Gaixia and Wujiang without reversing any sequence."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B has a dedicated personality section that names specific traits and ties them to concrete episodes (Yu Ji, Fan Zeng, massacres and burnings), while Draft A only lists traits in a short paragraph with few mapped examples."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B gives a dedicated analysis of the causes of success and failure, covering strategy, talent use, popular support and the contrast with Liu Bang, whereas Draft A's treatment is a brief summary with thin evidence."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B discusses the Shiji portrayal, later poets, Peking opera and the 'Ba Wang Bie Ji' legacy in more depth, while Draft A's discussion of later influence is cursory, though it presents a somewhat more balanced dual view."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft A misattributes the 'non-battle fault' quote to the Han Shu and paraphrases the Shiji's account of Xiang Yu's youth as a quote, while Draft B's episodes and quotations track the Shiji more closely, though it still contains minor date slips (e.g., 206 BCE for the war's start) and does not explicitly flag speculation."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B renders the turning points (Julu, Gaixia, Wujiang) with vivid scenes and quotations, though its closing grows rhetorical, while Draft A is restrained but too dry to meet the request for vivid, lively prose."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "tie", "why": "Both drafts state the exact title given in the request, and neither places it at the very top, since each has a short lead-in line before it."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A's passages walk through sampling, processing, culture, biochemical tests, virus extraction, PCR conditions and parasite preparation in order, with conditions stated at each step, while Draft B's passages cover only sampling and culture plus a reagent list."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B gives separate, detailed sections for the biochemical tests with judgment criteria, the virus EM and PCR procedures with reaction system and controls, and the parasite slide preparation with morphological indicators, whereas Draft A's sections are brief and lack controls and measurement details."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B correctly describes E. coli as a Gram-negative short rod, reports the WSSV band with positive, negative and marker controls, and gives Trichodina morphology including ciliary ring, denticle ring and size, while Draft A's Trichodina description is generic and lacks measurements and key structures."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B's analysis explains why each pathogen causes disease, notes the need for challenge tests and virulence-gene checks, and states the limits of biochemical and morphological identification, whereas Draft A's discussion mostly restates results and overclaims reliability."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "tie", "why": "Both drafts are written entirely in Chinese with Latin names and abbreviations kept as allowed, so neither is better on language."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A follows the life in clear chronological order with explicit dates for each stage, while Draft B is ordered but sketchier and less precise about timing."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A has a dedicated personality section covering bravery, loyalty, arrogance, and cruelty, tied to concrete episodes such as Hongmen, the killing of Song Yi, and the massacres, whereas Draft B's personality section is thin and its examples are weaker."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A gives a structured analysis of both the rise and the fall, with separate causes and comparisons to Liu Bang supported by episodes from the narrative, while Draft B's reasons are brief and less evidenced."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A covers the Shiji portrayal, poetic and dramatic reception (Li Bai, Du Mu, Peking opera), and the historical verdict in more depth, though it does not fully present competing views, while Draft B is more generic and omits drama."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A anchors most claims to quoted Shiji passages, though it misattributes the 赤泉侯 line to Julu and gives a wrong year for the alliance, while Draft B also contains errors (eight thousand troops at Julu, 千金一诺 and 分肉 presented as Shiji-based) and marks no speculation."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A uses vivid scene writing (the tent scene, the farewell with Yu Ji, the Wujiang refusal) and restrained commentary at the turning points, which fits the block better than Draft B's flatter, more summary tone."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A uses true screenplay conventions (INT./EXT. slug lines, character cues, parentheticals, action paragraphs), while Draft B is more of a markdown scene outline with italicized action."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A's comedy is more consistent and sharper (e.g., the 'product is air' jab and the 'surprise is the key ingredient of rom-coms' line), while Draft B's light humor is present but more conventional."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A names '爱之马卡龙' as Emily's signature and makes it drive the plot, since Mark's conversion comes from tasting it, and it recurs in the competition and the shop finale."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A builds the competition as a tense climax with a sudden oven failure, a rescue, a critic's reaction, and a clear award result, whereas Draft B's competition scenes are brief and mostly setup."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A shows Mark directly helping with the competition strategy and rescuing the oven, and the shop realized at the end is tied to his involvement, making his help central to the dream coming true."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A establishes Mark's stiff skepticism clearly, then shows a montage of them overcoming difficulties together, making his change of attitude and the growing bond feel gradual and believable."}, {"id": "r7", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A integrates both themes through plot and dialogue, using the 'bubble' dream motif and explicit lines about brave pursuit and love arriving unexpectedly, rather than only stating them at the close."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A follows a clear chronological sequence from birth through the uprising, Julu, Hongmen, Chu-Han war, Gaixia and Wujiang with consistent dates, while Draft B places the 208 capture of Xianyang before the 206 partition and mentions the Hongou agreement out of order."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A has a dedicated character section that ties traits like bravery, loyalty and indecision to specific episodes such as Hongmen, the killing of Song Yi and the refusal to cross the Wujiang, whereas Draft B stays generic with almost no textual examples."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A gives each cause of rise and fall a supporting episode from the sources, such as the Julu prestige, the Pengcheng battle, and the 'everywhere destroyed' comment on popular support, while Draft B lists four bare reasons without evidence."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A devotes separate sections to historical standing and to influence through the Shiji portrayal, the Wujiang suicide reception, and literary figures like Li Qingzhao and Du Mu, though it leans toward a single admiring verdict."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A anchors its key claims in quotations from the Shiji and does not commit the clear factual errors found in Draft B, though it does not explicitly flag speculation or note source contradictions."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A uses vivid scenes such as the Gaixia song and the Wujiang exchange and places measured commentary at the major turning points, while Draft B reads as a dry, generic summary."}]}

{"blocks": [{"id": "r1", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B uses standard INT./EXT. scene headings, a cast list, and clearly separated action and dialogue, which reads more like a real film script than Draft A's mixed Chinese-style scene labels."}, {"id": "r2", "winner": "A", "why": "Draft A delivers more comedic beats (the flour spill, the rent knock, the stuffed macaron, the parking excuse, the whisk-hand flirting), while Draft B's shown passages are drier and more business-serious."}, {"id": "r3", "winner": "tie", "why": "Both drafts name \"爱之马卡龙\" correctly as Emily's signature and use it to drive plot turns, such as softening Mark and anchoring the competition and shop."}, {"id": "r4", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B builds a clear third-act climax with a mid-competition oven failure, a critic's reaction, and a clear win, while Draft A's competition scenes are more perfunctory."}, {"id": "r5", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B shows Emily's shop realized and explicitly credits Mark's help (\"你帮我把泡泡变成了现实\"), whereas Draft A's ending centers on a proposal with little concrete evidence of Mark enabling the dream."}, {"id": "r6", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B shows Mark's skepticism, then a believable gradual softening through shared work and difficulties, while Draft A's romance has more visible flirting but a more abrupt attitude change."}, {"id": "r7", "winner": "B", "why": "Draft B states both themes in dialogue (\"勇敢去爱\", \"勇敢追求梦想的人\", \"真爱，也真的不期而遇了\"), while Draft A only gestures at the dream theme in a voiceover."}]}
